question: Should OpenClaw solve memory-wiki isolation with a generic per-agent plugin config contract, a memory-wiki-specific vault resolver, templated vault paths, or an explicit unsupported/shared-gateway policy?
rationale: This changes security-sensitive durable memory and plugin configuration semantics, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent API, migration, and no-context behavior.

options.title: Generic per-agent plugin config
options.body: Add a typed agents.list[].plugins override/merge contract and make memory-wiki consume it, coordinating with the broader #55401 use case.

options.title: Memory-wiki local resolver
options.body: Add a narrower memory-wiki-owned per-agent vault resolver first, accepting that other plugins still need separate follow-up design.

options.title: Document unsupported isolation
options.body: Keep one shared memory-wiki vault per gateway for now and document separate gateways or shared-public vaults as the supported isolation pattern.

recommendation.title: Generic per-agent plugin config
recommendation.body: Add a typed agents.list[].plugins override/merge contract and make memory-wiki consume it, coordinating with the broader #55401 use case.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision crosses plugin SDK/config compatibility and security boundaries where this history is strongest.
